title: Senator Rick Scott addresses national debt concerns in Washington Post letter - Duval Times
text:
Senator Rick Scott addressed the issue of rising government debt in a Letter to the Editor published by The Washington Post, as announced on Mar. 24. In his letter, Scott responded to a column by George Will about the increasing national debt, stating that its effects are already being felt by working Americans.
Scott said, “After the national debt hit $39 trillion, Will noted, as I have for years, that Congress’s reckless spending has put our country on the path to economic ruin.” He added that borrowing from future generations and paying interest to foreign countries like China is contributing to financial challenges and predicted that “We’ll likely hit the $40 trillion mark before November’s midterm elections.”
The senator emphasized his view that large-scale government intervention is making life more difficult for Americans. “Big government has made the cost of living explode and is threatening to destroy the American Dream. This is especially true for younger Americans, who have been royally screwed by Washington’s failures and the massive costs they’ve created,” Scott wrote.
Scott champions fiscal responsibility and policies supporting families and small businesses according to his official website. He also served on active duty in the U.S. Navy aboard USS Glover after high school according to his official website. Alongside his wife Ann, he raised two daughters and enjoys time with their grandchildren according to his official website.
Scott holds degrees in business from University of Missouri-Kansas City and law from Southern Methodist University according to his official website. He serves on several Senate committees including Armed Services; Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs; Budget; and Special Committee on Aging according to his official website. As reported by his office, he focused on economic growth during two terms as Florida governor and co-founded Columbia Hospital Corporation with Ann Scott according to his official website.
In closing remarks from his letter, Scott said: “This isn’t a problem to fix tomorrow; the ship is sinking today. If your representative in Congress thinks big government can fix it, vote them out.”
